newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrians begin voting in Euro and Vienna polls.
newsitem.headline: Austrians begin voting in Euro and Vienna polls.

text.p: Austrians began voting in a European parliamentary election on Sunday, in the first test of the government's popularity since a general election last December.

Some 5.8 million voters are eligible to vote in the first Euro-poll held in Austria to fill the 21 seats allocated to the Alpine republic in the Strasbourg-based European Parliament. Austria joined the European Union in January 1995.
Polling stations opened at 7 a.m. (0500 GMT) and will close at 6 p.m. (1600 GMT) when the first computer projections of the results were expected.

Voting in Vienna state elections also began with a little more than a million voters in the capital eligible to cast their ballot to determine the makeup of the country's richest and most powerful regional assembly.
Opinion polls have suggested the Social Democrats of Chancellor Franz Vranitzky could lose their majority control of Vienna for the first time since 1945.
